title: The TCP/IP Model: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: The T C P I P model describes the same journey as O S I. It just uses fewer layers. Four, to be exact.

scenes.heading: Letter in an envelope
scenes.narration: You write a letter, seal it, address it and post it. The application layer is you writing the letter. Transport is numbering the pages and tracking delivery. Internet is the address and the route. And network access is the van that carries it.

scenes.heading: Names for the data
scenes.narration: Each layer has its own name for the data. At the top it's just data. At transport, it's a segment. At the internet layer, it's a packet. And at the bottom, it's a frame and then bits.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three mix-ups. The Cisco model has four layers. A R P belongs at the link layer. And in T C P I P, encryption is handled at the application layer.
